title: Toolformer: Language Models That Use Tools
hook: Instead of hand-scripting when to call a calculator or search, Toolformer lets the model teach itself — try API calls during training, keep the ones that actually help.
key_points: The model learns when and how to call external tools, rather than being hand-scripted.
It tries candidate API calls in training text and keeps the ones that lower prediction loss.
Tools include things like a calculator, search engine, and question-answering API.
Trained in a self-supervised way from just a few examples per tool.
Improves performance while keeping the model's general language ability.
content_html: Toolformer, from Schick, Dwivedi-Yu, and colleagues at Meta in 2023, is a language model that learns to use external tools on its own. Rather than relying on hand-written rules for when to call a calculator, search engine, or API, it figures out useful calls during training and keeps the ones that improve its predictions. The result is learned, not scripted, tool use.
extra_html:
How it works

Toolformer takes plain text and inserts candidate API calls at various spots, then checks whether having the tool's result would help it predict the upcoming words. Calls that reduce its prediction loss are kept; the rest are discarded. The model is then fine-tuned on this self-annotated data, so it learns where to place calls and how to fold the returned results into its output — all from only a handful of examples per tool.

Why it matters

LLMs are weak at things like exact arithmetic or current facts that tools handle trivially. Toolformer showed a model can decide for itself when reaching for a tool pays off, without humans labeling every case. Because it's self-supervised, it scales to new tools cheaply, and it keeps the model's general abilities intact. It's an influential step toward agents that use tools natively rather than through brittle prompt rules.

related.title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
related.hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

prereqs.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
prereqs.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.
